title: Who keeps the shop clean
summary: Cleaning in Supermarket Simulator can be somebody else's job: the game defines a cleaning worker with their own item, a mop you can hold, and a generator for the people you employ.
body: There is a worker role for cleaning rather than one generic employee, which is why tidying up can be delegated once the shop is big enough.
The mop is an item of its own, so cleaning is something done with equipment rather than a menu command.
Cleaning has its own routine in the game, which is how a worker can keep going while you serve customers.
What this entry does not tell you: wages, how many people you may employ or how thorough a worker is. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There is a cleaning worker with an item of their own.
Cleaning is carried out by a routine of its own.
The people you employ are produced by the game.
The build ships a cleaner model, a cleaning marker and the rubbish bags the job produces.
facts.evidence: asset names: Cleaner_Wesh, Cleaning Arrow, Garbage_Bag_01_LOD0

facts.claim: More than one cleaner model is shipped, each named separately.
The shop has a janitor of its own, with a controller, an avatar, a ticket material and a janitorial supply named beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Janitor Controller, JanitorAvatar, Janitor_Ticket_Mat, SM_JanitorialSupply_LOD2
